items.title: Behind Trump's shift towards Russia, the lucrative business promises of Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's dealmaker
items.description: Kirill Dmitriev has been working to persuade the White House that peace in Ukraine must first come through commercial deals. Le Monde outlines two months that saw the new Russian-American partnership transform into an alliance against Kyiv, from Miami to Moscow.

items.title: How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war
items.description: Artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable. Russia and Ukraine both use AI-powered drones, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that AI could lead decisions on the battlefield as soon as next year.

items.title: Russian Drone Attack Kills 14 In Dnipro As Oleshky Truce Enters Third Day
items.description: A Russian attack on Ukraine's eastern city of Dnipro killed at least 14 people and injured more than 10 others, according to Ukrainian officials, as a fragile cease-fire around Russian-occupied Oleshky entered its third day on October 29.

items.title: After three years of civil war, Sudan faces the threat of inflation
items.description: Since May, the Sudanese pound has lost more than half of its value, pushing up food prices and putting more pressure on overstretched aid groups.

items.title: What would a new Israeli government mean for Arab neighbors? More of the same is expected, with some small positives predicted.
items.description: A new Israeli government is unlikely to bring big changes on Palestinian statehood and troops in Lebanon and Syria, experts say. Some small positives may be possible though.
